TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Diana Garcia, City Librarian
SUBJECT:  Appointment to the Library Board of Trustees

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council:
  1. Consider appointing one individual to fill the vacancy on the Library Board of
  Trustees; and
  2. Take such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

Membership on the City's Public Library Board of Trustees ("Library Board") are by
appointment of the City Council. Members appointed to the City's Library Board serve a
term of three yearsl; at the end of each term, the City Council may opt to either replace
or reappoint members. Members cannot serve more than two consecutive terms2. lt is
recommended that the City Council consider appointing one individual to fill the vacancy
on the Library Board.

BACKGROUND & DISCUSSION:

The Library Board is an administrative body established pursuant to the California
Education Code and Monterey Park Municipal Code ('MPMC'). The Library Board is
responsible for administering the Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library as well as all
library trust funds received by gift, bequest or devise.

MPMC Chapter 2.80 regulates the Library Board (in addition to applicable California
law). Specifically, Education Code S 18910 provides that:

  "[t]he public library shall be managed by a board of library trustees,
  consisting of five members, to be appointed by the mayor ... with the
  consent of the legislative body of the municipality."

This is reflected in MPMC S 2.80.020 which provides that:

1 Pursuant to Education  Code $ 18911
2 Ordinance Nos.2156 and 1880

  Page 3 of 17
 Staff Report
Page 2

  "[t]here is created and established a board of library trustees consisting of
  five members appointed by the mayor with the approval of the city
  council."

Pursuant to Education Code Section 18911, the term of office for a trustee is three
years; and no person may serve more than two consecutive terms as a member of the
board (see Ordinance Nos. 2156 and 1880).

There is one vacancy the Library Board, which was advertised of Trustees. ln response,
the City Clerk's office received three applications from residents interested in serving on
the Library Board: Jennifer Tang, Edmund Choi and Daisy Liu. lt is recommended that
the City Council consider appointing one of these three individual to fill the vacancy on
the Library Board.

FISCAL IMPACT:
None.

Honorable Mayor Liang, Mayor Pro-tem Chan, and Councilmembers

Thank you for your consideration of my application for the Library Board of Trustees. If selected, I would
be honored to serve the Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library, an institutional pillar in our community.

Below you will find my answers to questions provided by City Librarian Diana Garcia.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Love Tang

  1. Why are you interested in serving on the Monterey Park Bruggemeyer Library Board of
  Trustees?
  Whenever I patronize the Library, I see two things without fail: a parent checking out a gigantic
  stack ofbooks for their small child, and groups ofteenagers hanging out in a safe space. I am
  interested in serving on the Library Board of Trustees because I was that small child, I was that
  teenager, and I want to ensure our Library has the oversight and advocacy it needs to serve our
  community for generations to come.

  In my professional life, I am an English teacher. I am an expert in literacy, literature, and
  English-Learner education. I am also well-versed in social justice work, and since public libraries
  are a democratic equalizer (and the only place left in society where one can go without the
  expectation of having to pay money), I want to bring that lens to the board.

  2. Tell us about your prior volunteer service and/or experience serving on a Board.
  I curently serve as Vice President on the boards of the Monterey Park Democratic Club and the
  National Women's Political Caucus of the San Gabriel Valley. In these roles, I develop and
  coordinate programming for each organization on a monthly basis, as well as manage digital
  communication. Last year I organized a film screening at the Library for MPDC and recently our
  MPDC board raised $1250 for scholarships.

  During the Covid-19 crisis, I volunteered by coordinating food bank donations to the American
  Legion and the Alhambra Teachers Association, helped organize a Mothers' Day free meal pick
  up, and assisted in creating a mutual-aid network for individuals facing housing insecurity or job
  loss.

  Page 16 of 17
   In the past, I have volunteered to help high school students with college essays and coach youth
  on job interviews. I have participated in Mark Keppel High School's Career Day and various
  local neighborhood cleanups. Many moons ago, I was a regular volunteer under Mr. Costley in
  the Monterey Park City Hall.

3. What do you see as the role of the Board of Trustees in the community?
  Because the Board of Trustees are community members themselves, I see their job as an
  intermediary between the Library and the community, so that the Library continues to effectively
  serve the needs ofits patrons.

  Current and past Board Members have done a great job of this. Fbr instance, Mr. Dave Barron
  uses his media platforms to promote the good work happening at the Library, such as 3D printing
  PPE for medical workers and library staff checking in on senior citizens during the Covid-19
  crisis. Mr. Andy Yam has advocated for services for undocumented immigrants at the Library.
  These are just a few examples of the good work the Board and Library have already done, and I
  hope to build on thern.

4. How will you advocate for the interests of the library and its patrons?
  As a community organizer, I can easily engage with residents online and in-person (from a safe
  social distance, out in the neighborhood). I hope to utilize my organizing skills to elevate the
  needs ofLibrary patrons. Their needs should be heard and valued.

  I have also been a library patron for many years (especially now that I am boycotting Amazon
  whenever possible) and that firsthand experience is crucial in advocating for library patrons.

  I also hope to push the boundaries around what our Library can offer and find innovative ways
  further bring the institution into the 2l st century.

5. What are the characteristics of an effective Board member?
  I understand that Board positions can and should be grueling work. I understand it requires
  reading and thoroughly understanding what some may consider mundane - agendas, minutes,
  budgets, proposals, public correspondence. I did not apply for this position for a title or
  recognition. I did so because I want to help ensure our Library has long-term staying power. That
  means using oversight to ensure a healthy and sustainable budget. That means reacting to the
  changing needs of patrons. That means being an active board member putting in the work.

6. How can the Library Board of Trustees support and work with the Friends of the Library
  and the Library Foundation?
  All three of these bodies work in harmony. The Board should support the Friends of the Library
  and the Li*ary Foundation by actively promoting and attending fundraisers, helping to recruit
  volunteers, and generally working in coordination to ensure all programs are successful.

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JUNE 11, 2020

The City Council of the City of Monterey Park held a Special Teleconference Meeting on
Thursday, June 11, 2020 at 5:30 p.m. The special meeting was conducted pursuant to
Section 3 of Executive Order No. N-29-20 issued on March 17, 2020. Accordingly,
Council Members were provided a meeting login number and conference call number
and were not physically present at Council Chambers.

The minutes include items considered by the City Council acting on behalf of the
Successor Agency of the former Monterey Park Redevelopment Agency, which
dissolved February 1, 2012. Successor Agency matters will include the notation of “SA”
next to the Agenda Item Number.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

In accordance with Executive Order No. N-29-20 and guidance from the California
Department of Public Health on gatherings, remote public participation was allowed in
the following ways:

Participants were encouraged to join the meeting 30 minutes before the start of the
meeting.

Public comment was accepted via email to mpclerk@montereypark.ca.gov during the
meeting, before the close of public comment, and read into the record during public
comment, when feasible. We request that written communications be limited to not
more than 50 words.

Public comment may be submitted via telephone during the meeting, before the close of
public comment, by calling (888) 788-0099 or (877) 853-5247 and entering Zoom
Meeting ID: 99723992320 then press pound (#). When prompted to enter participation
ID number press pound (#) again. If participants would like to make a public comment
they will enter “*9” then the Clerk’s office will be notified and you will be in the rotation to
make a public comment.

The public may also watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T
U-verse, channel 99 or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s
website at http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos.

Important Disclaimer – When a participant calls in to join the meeting, their name
and/or phone number will be visible to all participants. Note that all public meetings will
be recorded.

1.  NEW BUSINESS

1.  APPOINTMENT TO THE LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES

  Membership on the City’s Public Library Board of Trustees (“Library Board”) are by
  appointment of the City Council. Members appointed to the City’s Library Board
  serve a term of three years1; at the end of each term, the City Council may opt to
  either replace or reappoint members. Members cannot serve more than two
  consecutive terms2. It is recommended that the City Council consider appointing
  one individual to fill the vacancy on the Library Board.

  Action Taken: The City Council appointed Jennifer Tang to fill the vacancy on the
